stem:
Which best combines the two sentences?

Mr. Santos is new to the office. He already knows all the rules.
choices: Although Mr. Santos is new to the office, he already knows all the rules.
Because Mr. Santos is new to the office, he already knows all the rules.
Mr. Santos is new to the office, so he already knows all the rules.
Mr. Santos is new to the office, he already knows all the rules.
answer: Although Mr. Santos is new to the office, he already knows all the rules.
hints: Read both sentences. Is the second one what you would expect after the first, or a surprise?
Someone new usually does not know all the rules yet. So the second idea is a surprise: it contrasts with the first.
Contrast words: although, but, even though. Cause words: because, so. Choose the sentence with a contrast word and correct punctuation.

solution.methodName: Find the link between the ideas, then check the grammar

steps.action: Find the link: a new employee usually does not know all the rules. Knowing them already is unexpected, so the ideas contrast.
steps.why: The word "already" is a clue that the second idea is a surprise.

steps.action: First choice: "Although" shows contrast, and a comma correctly ends the "although" part. Correct.
Second choice: "Because" says being new is the reason he knows the rules. That makes no sense. Wrong.
Third choice: "so" also shows cause and effect. Wrong link.
Fourth choice: a comma alone joins two complete sentences. This is a comma splice. Wrong.
The answer is "Although Mr. Santos is new to the office, he already knows all the rules."

trapNotes.Because Mr. Santos is new to the office,: The grammar is fine, but "because" says being new caused him to know the rules. The real link is a contrast.
trapNotes.Mr. Santos is new to the office, so he a: "So" is a correct joining word, but it shows a result. Knowing the rules is not a result of being new.
trapNotes.Mr. Santos is new to the office, he alre: It keeps the meaning, but it joins two complete sentences with only a comma. That is a comma splice.
